61a354.conditions: 49-byte subscripts exceed the 32-byte inline sync data, so each server-to-server SUBSCRIBE (server 3 -> 2) and NOTIFY (server 2 -> 3) is a sync header plus a separate ADLB_TAG_SYNC_SUB message; the crash needs both to arrive after the receiver's MPI_Test on the sync ring and before its MPI_Iprobe(ANY_SOURCE, ANY_TAG)
61a354.reasoning: In serve_several the server first tests the head of the preposted sync Irecv ring, then calls xlb_poll: MPI_Iprobe(MPI_ANY_SOURCE, MPI_ANY_TAG). send_subscribe_sync Isends the header, then does a blocking SEND of the subscript tagged ADLB_TAG_SYNC_SUB, which is meant to be received only by the RECV in xlb_handle_subscribe_sync or enqueue_deferred_notify. If header and subscript both arrive during the Iprobe's progress, the header completes the ring Irecv without being seen, and the probe returns the SYNC_SUB message as the oldest unexpected one. xlb_handle has no handler for that tag, so ADLB_CHECK_MSG fails ('invalid tag'), ADLB_Server returns an error and the driver calls MPI_Abort. When the header is noticed first (it usually is), the run succeeds. Separately, with unbuffered sends the two servers' blocking SYNC_SUB SENDs to each other can deadlock.
